lines.crawler3d.setting.turns.help: Real time: each one acts when its gauge fills, and the monsters do not wait. Turns: the vaults wait for you; each step, turn or blow is a turn

notes.crawler3d.boot: A step on the loading screen while the game builds the vaults.
notes.crawler3d.name.bram: The four in the party: Bram the fighter, Tesk the rogue, Maren the cleric, Quill the mage. Keep the names, or write them in your letters.
notes.crawler3d.compass.n: The compass over the view: north, east, south, west, one letter each.
notes.crawler3d.card: A party member's card: {n} is the number key that makes them act (1 to 4), then their name.
notes.crawler3d.down: On a party member's card when their life is gone (knocked out).
notes.crawler3d.turn.yours: In the Turns setting: the party may act. THEIR TURN: the monsters act. REAL TIME: the other setting, where nobody waits.
notes.crawler3d.map.title: Over the big map: the place's name and then {key}, which is IRON KEY once the party carries it, else nothing.
notes.crawler3d.map.key: On the big map: the party carries the iron key.
notes.crawler3d.say.intro: The first message: the Lantern Vaults are the dungeon (its name may be translated); the stair out is at the bottom.
notes.crawler3d.say.warden_hall: The Warden is the dungeon's boss, an armoured guardian; its hall is the last room.
notes.crawler3d.say.gate_stuck: The party bumps a closed gate: something else (a lever, a plate) raises it.
notes.crawler3d.say.grinding: A plate in the floor stepped on: a gate rises somewhere far away.
notes.crawler3d.say.key: The iron key just picked up.
notes.crawler3d.say.flask: A healing flask just picked up: everyone in the party heals.
notes.crawler3d.say.locked: The locked gate: the party has no iron key yet.
notes.crawler3d.say.heals: {healer} is the cleric's name, {name} the one healed.
notes.crawler3d.say.falls: A party member's life is gone.
notes.crawler3d.say.sweep: The Warden hits the whole front rank (the two in front) at once.
notes.crawler3d.over.lost: The end screen after the whole party falls: one sentence over two rows (the \n breaks the row; keep one).
notes.crawler3d.over.won: The title over the end screen when the party climbs the stair out.
notes.crawler3d.over.climb: The end screen after the win: how many of the party ({party}, four) are still alive. Another stat follows on the same row.
notes.crawler3d.over.foes: The end screen: how many monsters the party killed.
notes.crawler3d.touch.spell: The touch button for the mage's fire bolt. Keep it short (about 5 letters).
notes.crawler3d.setting.turns: A setting in the pause menu: whether the game plays in real time or turn by turn.
notes.action.strafe_l: A control's name on the controls screen: step aside to the left (l is left). Keep it short.
notes.action.strafe_r: A control's name on the controls screen: step aside to the right (r is right).
notes.action.act: A control's name on the controls screen, and in capitals on its touch button: use what is in front (a lever, a gate) or attack.
notes.action.spell: A control's name: the mage casts a fire bolt down the corridor.
notes.action.heal: A control's name, and in capitals on its touch button: the cleric heals the most hurt.
notes.action.m1: A control's name: party member 1 acts (M for member). M 2, M 3 and M 4: the others.

brief: The 3D crawler slice: a first-person dungeon crawl like Wizardry or Dungeon Master: a party of four (two fighters in front, a cleric and a mage behind) moves a cell at a time through the Lantern Vaults, pulling levers, finding an iron key, dodging darts, and fights the Warden at the bottom. The messages are short, in capitals, like an old dungeon game's log; they speak of the party, never to one hero (the player is the party, unnamed).
